Changelog

v2.0, 2026-11-06

  • Steps: nine steps (Intro, Text, Page, Margins, Columns, Typography, Styles, Report, Download) shown as one continuous sentence with the current step highlighted, step numbers as superscripts. Back and Next sit centred under the page with the step name above Next. The Report replaces the page area.
  • Intro: opens with a large-type description on the page stage, black on the light stage with no card. It names the steps as dashed-underlined links with superscript numbers, says to read the text and understand its structure first, and says the work is trial and error. The start screen is called chase, with a large yellow title. The page behind it shows the Bringhurst essay running over several pages, whatever has been typed on the Text step.
  • Text: typed or pasted into the text box, or loaded from a file (txt, md, html, docx, odt, rtf) or dropped onto it. Files are read in the browser and not uploaded; PDF is not supported yet. Word, OpenDocument and html files keep Heading 1 to 3, quotes, italics and line breaks, and edited text is not replaced by a file without asking. The box has style buttons (H1, H2, H3, Quote, Source, Italic) with shortcuts, a Break button and Shift+Enter for a soft return, an icon that opens it as a large editor, and a how-to guide for the marks.
  • Marks in the text set styles: # ## ### for Heading 1 to 3, > for Block Quote, -- for Citation (set with an em dash), *text* for Emphasis (italic), and a backslash at the end of a line for a soft return. The page preview shows the styles and does not draw the marks.
  • Styles: named type hierarchy (Heading 1 to 3, Block Quote, Citation, Emphasis) with a size ratio and a typeface for each style. Headings are set tight and padded to whole lines so the text stays on the baseline grid. The step lists only the styles the text uses and prompts back to the Text step.
  • Paragraphs are separated by a space after, set in points (default 14 pt), not by empty lines. Blank lines are ignored, and pasted or imported text drops them.
  • Columns: a visual picker (stepper plus equal-width column blocks, yellow for the text box) sets the number of columns, the text box span and where the text starts, with one icon per column. Columns that leave no room for the span are greyed out. Text flows from one column to the next; facing pages show the same text on both pages. In the ragged edge view the gutters are filled black.
  • Typography: ten system fonts in classified groups, and the selection changes the page text. Left aligned and justified icons, a hyphenation icon in the Alignment row, and the ragged edge and rivers views.
  • Report: Considerations replace Warnings. Line length, type size and leading, and counts of orphans, widows and runts, are shown as plain text when in range and as warnings with reasons for particular readers when not. The Patrick says block is removed.
  • Help: a ? in the panel header turns on tap-to-read tooltips; controls with tooltips are outlined and tapping shows the text instead of acting. Tooltips are in plainer language.
  • Phone: the panel is a bottom sheet, resting at half height; pushing up lifts it over the page and then the content scrolls; pulling down lowers or folds it. The folded panel stays at the bottom, the page area ends above it so Back and Next stay clear, and the pop-out is hidden.
  • Panel: follows Form's pattern, with a fixed header holding the View icons (text, margins, columns, solid fills, ragged edge) on one row with an em / mm choice, section cards, a sticky foot, and Form's handle for folding. The scale reading is in the foot. Number fields have real minus and plus steppers; single and facing page icons; margin link toggle; links in panel text are yellow.
  • Preview: drawn in real pixels so Safari shows text at the right size. It fits the browser height for portrait pages; facing and landscape pages fit the width and scroll. Margins and columns guides are yellow and cycle off, outline, solid on repeated clicks. A baseline grid toggle shows lines at the leading of the first column's text, visible with more than one column. Icons pop the page and the text editor out into their own windows and back; the pop-out is not shown on the intro.
  • PDF: page 1 a clean text-only page, page 2 a vector grid page with measurements in millimetres and ems, then the specification, which lists paragraph and character styles. Page text no longer exports italic.
  • IDML: Download for InDesign with named paragraph styles and an Emphasis character style, forced line breaks for soft returns, per-style typeface, baseline alignment and keep with next, and CMYK swatches only. It ends with a specification page: a table of each setting, its value, and where to change it in InDesign (menu path, Mac and Windows shortcut), with a File > Open note and how to show or hide the baseline grid and switch off align to grid.
  • Reset also resets styles, the text box span and start, alignment (to left), the Report and the download area.
  • About text updated for the feature set. The calculator is called Composition, the site chase. Em link replaced (Em sizing).

v1.0, 2026-11-05

  • chase calculates multi-column page layouts. A page size, margins, columns and a type size give column widths, gutters and line lengths on Bringhurst's principles, drawn as a page.
  • The calculator works in seven steps: intro, text, page, margins, columns, type, then the download of the specification as a PDF.
  • A GREP generator builds InDesign GREP patterns for words, digits, punctuation and enclosed text.
  • A start screen with an About drawer introduces the tooling, in the same shell as Form.
